thread:
Benita: hey team, i'm Benita (platform eng) and i'm on-call for the first time next week. quick list of items i couldn't find and a few process q's.
Aly: welcome Benita! short answers usually work best here. fire away.
Benita: 1) vendor escalation: if we think the issue is a managed infra problem (e.g., GCE networking), what's the canonical path to escalate to GCP? do we page them directly or go through a Redwood account rep?
Aly: we do NOT page vendors directly. flow is: primary oncall -> @ops-security/pager for external-impact consent -> we open a partner escalation ticket via the vendor portal using the company escalation token. the owning SRE or EM must approve before we hand over PII or internal traces. ops-security will help.
ops-security: adding detail: before vendor contact, sanitize logs (remove ip/host identifiers), and create a redacted bundle using `tools/redact.sh`. if you need a vendor-esc row in PD, use the `vendor_escalation` option in the incident form so the audit log shows consent.
Benita: good to know. 2) i sometimes need to run perf profiling on a prod pod for a tricky leak. what's the process for temporary elevated access to run pprof/perf?
Max: short: request ephemeral sudo via the privilege workflow. steps: 1) open access request at https://internal.redwood/priv-requests with justification, 2) tag @ops-security and the owning EM, 3) request TTL (we usually give 1h). we log sessions via bastion and require session recording. do NOT copy creds out.
Benita: is there a CLI example for requesting ephemeral creds?
Max: yes, we have a small helper:
```
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/priv-requests \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"resource":"prod-bastion","duration":"1h","reason":"profiling leak"}'
```
ops-security: we prefer the web form so approvals are traceable, but the API exists for automation.
Benita: 3) i need to swap one of my shifts because of a timezone conflict. what's the swap policy and how do i ensure coverage?
Aly: use the PD swap feature and cc @sre-training. for swaps within 48h, you must also DM your buddy and confirm before you finalize the swap. PD will block swaps that leave gaps. note: for swaps to someone outside your rotation pool, get EM approval.
sre-training: i can add a shadow for your swapped shift if you want extra coverage. want me to do that?
Benita: yes please. i'll need a shadow for the first 2 swapped pages.
sre-training: done, assigned @Max as your shadow for those two shifts.
Benita: 4) runbooks: some of our runbooks include snippets that require access to a credentials vault. where do i get ephemeral read-only secrets for the runbook steps?
ops-security: use the secrets broker (https://secrets.redwood/internal) with an auditable grant. request via the runbook's `request-secret` link or our CLI:
```
secrets-cli request --name runbook-prod-db --ttl 15m --purpose "triage"
```
We log requests and require justification in PD incident notes.
Benita: 5) can simulated pages accidentally hit vendor escalation hooks or automation? i don't want to trigger rollbacks or vendor calls during tests.
Aly: sims are safe by default. PD simulated incidents set `simulated:true` metadata; all our automation checks that flag before executing. vendor_escalation is disabled for simulated incidents. still, please do sims in low-traffic windows and notify the team.
Benita: awesome. last: any short checklist for first-time primaries? a printable 4-step would be great.
Max: here you go: 1) acknowledge in PD + note "shadowed by @Max" if applicable, 2) run top-level runbook steps, 3) check recent deploys + CI pipelines, 4) if >15m to mitigation, @-mention EM + ops-security and start incident doc.
Benita: thanks — i'll try a simulated page tomorrow at 03:00 UTC to test SSO and shadow flag. ok to run?
Aly: fine, i'll be around. tag this thread when you start the sim. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Reminder: complete oncall quickstart checklist at https://internal.redwood/oncall-quickstart.
Benita: noted. opening a priv-req and secrets request now. thanks everyone!
